abstract: <jats:p>Operational optimization of activated sludge plants requires repeated solutions of coupled biological, recycle, and settling equations. Statistical surrogates can reduce this computational cost, but their predictions must respect the physical connections among treatment units. This study develops a plant-wide, physically constrained statistical surrogate that combines second- order ridge regression with joint quadratic projection. The model predicts mixer and reactor concentrations, clarifier outlet component flows, and stored solids. Projection enforces the specified component and inventory balances, separation requirements, inventory bounds, and non-negativity. A simulated plant with five reactors and a ten-layer clarifier provides 7,386 accepted development states and 1,845 accepted holdout states. Projection reduces aggregate normalized root mean square error by 8.19% and normalized mean absolute error by 15.65%. Root mean square error improves in 30 of the 32 combinations of treatment location and water-quality measure. Surrogate-based operating searches are compared with direct smooth mechanistic optimization for a nominal influent and ten additional influent scenarios. Retained decisions are evaluated by independently solving the original mechanistic equations at the selected controls. Direct optimization gives a lower reference-model objective in all eleven retained comparisons. Across the ten influent scenarios, mean optimization times are 1.726 s for the surrogate and 5.236 s for the direct route. These times exclude model development and subsequent verification. The contribution is a connected plant surrogate that enforces specified physical relations and supports faster operating searches. The results also show that physical consistency and favorable average accuracy do not establish decision quality, which requires mechanistic evaluation.</jats:p>
title: Plant-wide Optimization of Activated Sludge Systems Using a Physically Constrained Statistical Surrogate
